prompt.context: The Philadelphia Museum of Art (a for-profit institution) has a web site that is basically set up just for users to look at. The head of the museum feels that there must be some way to increase the museum's revenues through use of the web site, and so he asks you to explore this issue as part of your summer research project.
prompt.question: What do you recommend to the head of the museum?

clarifying_info.q: How does the museum generate revenue currently?
clarifying_info.a: Currently, the museum earns revenues from membership fees, entrance fees, catalog sales, and corporate sponsorship of blockbuster shows. Blockbuster shows are major art exhibitions that are sponsored by companies when the collections come to town. For example, a blockbuster show might be called the 'US AIR' presentation of Monet's Garden at Giverny.

framework: Focus only on revenues (not costs), since the question specifically asks how to increase revenues
Split into two buckets: (1) use the web site to increase sales of existing products and services, and (2) use the web site to market and sell new products and services

questions.prompt: How can the web site be used to boost revenue from existing sources?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm enhancements to each existing revenue stream — catalog sales, membership fees, entrance fees, and corporate sponsorship — using the web as a channel. Strong answers address online catalog ordering with credit-card checkout and fulfillment logistics, advertising the museum's regular and blockbuster events to drive entrance-fee and membership-fee revenue, and allowing customers to join as members directly on the web.

questions.prompt: What new revenue streams could the web site enable?
questions.guidance: Candidate should generate creative, web-native ideas beyond the existing revenue categories, e.g., member-only online chat groups about art (incremental value to justify higher or new membership tier), and selling advertising spots on the web site to relevant, curated brands (screening out inappropriate advertisers).

brainstorming.prompt: What specific ideas do you have for each of the two buckets (existing sources and new sources)?

categories.name: Boost existing revenue streams via web
ideas: Online catalog ordering — allow customers worldwide to browse and purchase museum memorabilia and gifts without needing a physical catalog or visiting the store; handle payment by credit card and fulfillment via logistics partner (e.g., FedEx)
Actively address consumer security concerns about online credit card transactions; offer fraud guarantees

Advertise museum collections, regular exhibitions, and blockbuster shows through the web site; use hotlinks from corporate sponsor pages (e.g., US AIR homepage), local/national tourism sites (e.g., www.boston.com)
Allow customers to sign up for museum membership directly and conveniently on the web rather than having to be on-site or call during office hours

categories.name: Create new web-native revenue streams
ideas: Member-only or paid chat groups/online communities around art topics — adds value to membership tier or creates a standalone paid service
Sell targeted advertising spots on the museum's web site to appropriate, curated companies (art supplies, travel, culture — screen out irrelevant brands)

recommendation: Use the web site to enhance revenues from existing sources: enable online catalog sales and streamline membership sign-up, and leverage advertising and hotlinks to drive entrance-fee and membership-fee revenue
Use the web site to generate new revenue: launch member online communities (chat groups) and sell tastefully screened advertising spots to relevant brands
risks: Consumer resistance to sharing credit card details online — must invest in security messaging and fraud guarantees
Brand risk from inappropriate advertisers on site — requires rigorous screening process
New digital initiatives require upfront investment in web development and customer education
next_steps: Conduct a cost-benefit analysis for each initiative (web store build-out, ad platform setup)
Pilot the online catalog store and measure conversion rates before full roll-out
Develop an advertiser screening policy and rate card for web advertising spots
